note: Naqada's -3200 keyframe drops the desert governorates the gazetteer region 'Lower Egypt' carries (Matruh, 524 cells, and the Giza desert, about 100); the Delta, the Cairo reach and the Faiyum, where the Maadian sites lay, stay.

union.text: the Delta, the Cairo-Giza valley reach and the Faiyum, where the Maadian sites lay: Maadi near modern Cairo, Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha; without the desert governorates of Matruh and the Giza oases

correction.text: the Nile valley of Upper Egypt plus the Maadian lands it took over, the Delta, Cairo and the Faiyum, without the Matruh and Giza desert

keyframe_overrides.why: Maadi culture page: 'The cultures of Lower Egypt were replaced by Upper Egypt and Naqada culture by the end of Naqada II circa 3200 BCE'; the culture 'consists in about a dozen sites, including the excavated cemetery and settlement complex Maadi near modern Cairo' (Buto, Tell el-Farkha, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, el-Gerza, Haraga, Abusir el-Melek, Minshat Abu Omar) and the page names no site in the Western Desert or on the Matruh coast. The dossier's correction uses the gazetteer's 'Lower Egypt' (787 cells), of which Matruh alone is 524 and the Giza desert about 100; the corrected shape keeps the 180 cells of the Delta, the Cairo-Giza Nile reach and the Faiyum.
